name: Duke Energy
scope1Precision: Calculated sum of nine rounded Scope 1 components, not a separately reported exact total.
unit: tCO₂e / 1,000 qualifying baseline methane tonnes CO₂e
boundary: Qualifying vented pipeline methane, after recovered-methane combustion; compressor and other lifecycle effects excluded
summary: Gas normally vented during suitable planned maintenance can be moved into another pipeline. Established recovery methods reduce methane loss while preserving safe maintenance and gas delivery. Duke’s remaining eligible events are not identified.
formula: 1,000 × 50% recovery × (29.8 − 2.75) / 29.8 = 453.86 tCO₂e; upper technical case at 90% recovery = 816.95 tCO₂e
opportunity: Screen untreated scheduled blowdowns for recovery equipment and service contracts.
constraints: The 50–90% recovery evidence is an EPA industry benchmark, not measured remaining Duke opportunity or a universal guarantee.
Duke’s 393,000 tCO₂e gas methane inventory includes other sources and cannot be used as the blowdown baseline.
Required pipeline connections, pressures, maintenance time and reliable service must match; emergency events may be unsuitable.
Recovered methane is assumed completely burned. Compressor energy, leakage, equipment impacts and other hydrocarbons remain unquantified; no displacement credit is taken.
Already recovered or flared events are excluded from an untreated venting baseline. Eligible extent and financing additionality are unknown.
The inventory uses company reporting factors; the separate normalized methane comparison uses AR6 fossil methane 29.8. Do not silently mix those factors.
sources: Technology · EPA pump-down lessons, pp. 1–3 and 7
Methane GWP · IPCC AR6 WGIII Annex II Table 11
Operating context · Duke EEI/AGA gas template, p. 3 (2024 data)
steps: Sum the nine rounded 2025 Scope 1 rows to obtain approximately 80.703 million tonnes CO₂e.
Identify still-vented maintenance events that can maintain required pipeline service using recovery. No eligible company total is established.
EPA gives 50–90% recovery in suitable circumstances. Normalize to 1,000 tonnes of otherwise vented methane climate burden.
Subtract complete combustion of the recovered methane: 2.75 tonnes CO₂ per tonne methane. The 50% case gives about 454 tonnes CO₂e before other lifecycle effects.
